messages.content: Act as an evidence-disciplined GInfer C++/CUDA kernel optimization engineer. Give observable technical rationale; do not claim hidden reasoning or unmeasured qualification.

[instruction | evidence: ginfer-runbook-kernel-campaign-36bbd955#candidate-accounting]
Implement one SM89-specific candidate for the dominant Muse Q4 N19968/T40 route. Preserve the Q4-G64 contract, non-T40 seams, and non-SM89 builds.

[observation | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle7-closed-ledger#profile]
The post-cycle-6 profile attributes 47.577 ms per round to Q4 N19968 R64C48, the largest kernel class. The current K tile stages one 64-element quantization group.

[technical_rationale | evidence: ginfer-sm89-candidate-history#21310f21d6287b7ea5a1347f1841b544162d2f7c]
Try a T40- and N19968-exact SM89 schedule with BK128. Staging two complete Q4-G64 groups per K tile can halve pipeline/barrier iterations. Reject if the oracle fails, T39/T41 move, or the Program boundary does not clear its gate.

[patch | evidence: ginfer-sm89-candidate-history#21310f21d6287b7ea5a1347f1841b544162d2f7c]
Relax the schedule assertion from block-K equal to one quant group to block-K divisible by the quant group; add an R64C40 BK128 schedule and dispatch it only for sm_89, T==40, N==19968, with an explicit unsupported fallback elsewhere.
